name: Malinda Lo
knownFor: Author of Ash, a sapphic Cinderella, and Last Night at the Telegraph Club.
bio: Malinda Lo is an American writer of young-adult novels. She was born in China and moved to the United States at the age of three; she graduated from Wellesley College, took a master's degree in Regional Studies from Harvard, and left Stanford's anthropology programme with a second master's. She also researches diversity in young-adult literature and publishing.

Her first novel, Ash (2009), reworks Cinderella with a lesbian heroine, and her later fantasy and science-fiction books include Huntress, Adaptation and Inheritance. Last Night at the Telegraph Club (2021), a historical romance about a Chinese American teenager discovering her sexuality in 1950s San Francisco, is her best-known book.

works.title: Ash
works.note: a lesbian reworking of Cinderella; a finalist for the Lambda Literary Award

works.title: Last Night at the Telegraph Club
works.note: set in San Francisco's Chinatown during the McCarthy-era Red Scare; won the National Book Award for Young People's Literature

events.text: Published her first novel, Ash, which was a finalist for the William C. Morris Award and the Lambda Literary Award, among others.
Served on the faculty of the Lambda Literary Foundation's Writer Retreat for Emerging LGBT Voices.
Wrote the short story that became Last Night at the Telegraph Club, for an anthology of queer teen stories.
Published Last Night at the Telegraph Club on 19 January.
Named by Carnegie Corporation of New York as an honoree of the Great Immigrants Awards.

relevance: Ash is one of the best-known fairy-tale retellings with a lesbian heroine, and Last Night at the Telegraph Club is a major historical sapphic romance: a love story that is also the story of queer life in Chinese American San Francisco before Stonewall.
influence: Her books have brought sapphic stories to a young-adult readership and to the major awards for young people's literature.
